clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of left lower abdominal lump, pain, and intermittent fever with chills. Vaginal examination revealed a 10x8.5 cm left lower abdomen mass. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen showed a heterogeneous enhancing solid cystic lesion with septations measuring 10x9.5x9.0 cm in the left ovary. Surgical excision revealed a specimen of 11x9x8.5 cm with cystic and solid areas and black pigmentation. Histopathology with H&E and PAS stains revealed dense inflammation, necrosis, and florid fungal septate hyphae with dichotomous branching consistent with Aspergillus infection. The patient was treated with intravenous voriconazole and liposomal amphotericin B for 10 days. Microbiological or molecular confirmation and post-treatment clinical outcome were not documented.
